criterion_scores.reasoning: The high-level two-stage design is sound: metadata discovery, allowlist-only body reads, no write tools in the distill subagent, HITL gates, denylist checks, and loud Supabase-key failure are all present. However, the final write instructions contain load-bearing contradictions: B5 reintroduces title/date/kind dedup despite B3 identifying URL-keyed dedup as critical, and Stage A treats snippets as metadata despite the no-body/no-PII boundary. These are core behavioral issues in a producer skill, so correctness is below the pass line.

Most required parts are present at useful depth: inputs, Stage A worksheets, Stage B extraction, entity resolution, write gate, write steps, labeling/idempotency, failure modes, and references. The major completeness gap is that the final write payload does not actually carry the all-sources/source_count provenance required by the cross-newsletter merge design, so an implementer following B5 would not realize the earlier B3.5 contract.

The skill is correctly placed/named for a project skill, has frontmatter, avoids alex: prefix, keeps MCP writes in the parent thread, and keeps the distill subagent write-less. The major convention defect is the direct REST company write path in B5, which bypasses the single guarded spine write path documented by the artifact's own ADR-9 section and by house convention.

The design is generally lean and safety-oriented, with HITL gates and abstention rather than speculative automation. But the artifact preserves two incompatible write procedures: direct REST writes in the operational section and guarded spine_write/spine_client writes in the ADR-9 section. That stale/duplicated contract is exactly the kind of drift that produces unsafe bypasses and false confidence.

The artifact is unusually legible, with explicit failure modes, coverage honesty requirements, label gotchas, and confidence/gap notes. Diagnostics are weakened by field-name drift between canonical_url and primary_url and by environment-specific 'validated' Gmail write-scope claims without a cited/reproducible validation record. Failures would mostly be explicable, but these inconsistencies would cost reviewer time.

This contradicts the later ADR-9 section in the same artifact, which says inbox signal writes and manual writes go through the single guarded write path.

defects.quote: Dedup on (title, event_date::date, kind) as a backstop.
defects.description: The write step reintroduces a title/date/kind dedup key even though B3 says canonical_url is the primary dedup key and explains that company/kind/date-style keys falsely merge distinct same-day events. As written, the implementation guidance can still produce the exact false-merge the skill says is load-bearing to avoid.

defects.spec_ref: Artifact B3.5 lines 137-139 and B4 lines 151-152
defects.description: The final event payload drops the merged cross-newsletter provenance promised earlier. B3.5 says one event should carry all citing newsletters in metadata.sources plus source_count, but the write payload collapses sources to a generic ["inbox"] and omits source_count, losing a required part of the run-batched dedup design.

defects.quote: Never use the Supabase MCP (wrong account). Base `https://oicikjyzmxqfomrrqkvf.supabase.co/rest/v1`; headers `apikey`/`Authorization: Bearer`/`Content-Type`/`Prefer: return=representation`.
defects.spec_ref: House convention: single guarded write path; artifact ADR-9 Write path lines 221-224
defects.description: The skill keeps an older direct-REST write recipe alive while also documenting a newer guarded write path later. Maintaining two incompatible write contracts is a stale-procedure/duplicated-state anti-pattern and increases the chance that future runs bypass the write-side denylist/PII guard.

The extraction schema names the required field canonical_url, while this write step uses primary_url. The surrounding prose also alternates between canonical_url and primary_url. The intent is understandable, but the field-name mismatch makes failures harder to diagnose and invites implementation drift.

defects.spec_ref: Artifact ground rules lines 20-22; Stage A goal lines 37-40
defects.description: The skill classifies Gmail snippets as metadata during the Stage A no-body discovery pass. Snippets are content excerpts and can contain private text; although line 48 later says the boundary filter retains no snippet/body, this line weakens the Stage A safety boundary and could lead an implementer to treat snippets as safe metadata.

defects.quote: The connector is read+write as of the 2026-09-10 reauth (`gmail.modify` + `gmail.labels`).
defects.description: This environment-specific operational claim is stated as validated without pointing to a run log or reproducible check. The section does include a later instruction to re-resolve IDs and probe label writes, so this is a documentation/provenance nit rather than a hard confidence-honesty cap.

checks_performed: Checked skill frontmatter/name/path against project-skill conventions, including no alex: prefix.
Checked the Stage A/Stage B flow for the advertised safety boundary: metadata-only discovery, allowlist-only body reads, denylist/boundary filtering, and human approval gates.
Checked write paths against house constraints: subagents do not write, MCP writes stay in parent thread, and spine writes should use the single guarded spine_write/spine_client path.
Checked entity resolution, canonical URL handling, deduplication, and cross-newsletter merge behavior for internal consistency.
Checked PII/logging/provenance claims against the actual fields and worksheet/write payloads specified in the skill.
Checked failure modes and diagnostics for loud failures, honest coverage reporting, and stale/unverified operational claims.
Checked supplied deterministic reference/tombstone results: no verified-missing .claude references and no live removed-tool hits were supplied.
